records.text: Turning Point USA prerecorded its All-American Halftime Show a couple of weeks before the live Super Bowl halftime performance.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We should be clear it was a prerecord. ... so Bad Bunny was performing live, ... Turning Point USA prerecorded, I think, a couple of weeks ago.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting confirms the program was prerecorded in Atlanta rather than broadcast live. The transcript itself hedges the recording date with 'I think,' and no authoritative source located establishes that it was recorded specifically a couple of weeks earlier.

sources.title: Us Weekly: All-American Halftime Show was prerecorded
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous report confirming the show was pretaped in Atlanta.

records.text: The All-American Halftime Show reached more than 10 million concurrent views across its social channels at one point.
records.speaker: Andrew Kolvet

appearances.snippet: Yeah, it was a kind of blew our minds actually a little bit, Brian (show host; surname unverified). ... And we saw at one point across all the different social channels, we saw over 10 million concurrent views.

verification.notes: AP independently observed roughly 5 million concurrent YouTube viewers and records Kolvet's estimate of roughly 10 million across all social platforms, but TPUSA did not release the exact cross-platform figures requested by AP. No independent aggregate analytics were available to establish that concurrent viewership exceeded 10 million.

records.text: More than 20 million Americans tuned in to the All-American Halftime Show.
records.speaker: Andrew Kolvet

appearances.snippet: What we can safely say is over 20 million Americans tuned in to the All-American Halftime Show tonight.

verification.notes: The official YouTube upload now shows more than 20 million accumulated views, but accumulated plays are not unique live viewers or necessarily Americans. AP reported that TPUSA did not release an exact platform breakdown, so more than 20 million American viewers cannot be established from public evidence.

records.text: Andrew Kolvet lied about the All-American Halftime Show's concurrent YouTube audience, and the claimed figure is impossible.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), ... Do you have a sense of how many people watched? ... over 10 million concurrent views. ... I was just in awe that they were going to try to sell this, that they were going to do what he did with his face and just lie and pretend that 6 million, ... that's just not true on its face. ... I'm going to walk you through this so you don't even have to have my background on YouTube to understand why this number is impossible.

verification.notes: The preceding Fox clip attributes roughly 10 million concurrent viewers to all social platforms, not six million on YouTube alone; AP independently observed roughly 5 million concurrent YouTube viewers. The statement therefore misstates Kolvet's claim, and neither a deliberate lie nor impossibility is established. YouTube also warns that live/public metrics can temporarily freeze or change while engagement is validated.

records.text: A screenshot showing 5,839 views and 175 comments but 667,000 likes for the All-American Halftime Show reflects made-up metrics.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This is a screenshot of their viewership after 6 million people tuned in concurrently at the exact same time. So that was 6 million people watching like we have 95,000 people watching right now on YouTube. ... 5,839 views with 175 comments. ... That is an impossible metric. ... But 667,000 likes. This is made up. But again,

verification.notes: The screenshot appears in the episode, but a transient mismatch among views, comments, and likes is not evidence that the numbers were fabricated. YouTube states that public metrics may update at different times and can freeze or change during validation; no platform audit or other direct evidence proving fabrication was found.

records.text: The All-American Halftime Show's reported total of over 20 million views with only 46,000 comments is fabricated.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: over 20 million views and yet only 46,000 comments it's impossible it's just it's it's literally made up like I said you know that the Erika (Erika Kirk) address is an authentic representation of views because of the views to comments ratio I'll give you an example my last episode the letter to Erika (Erika Kirk) on YouTube that got 3.1 million views it has 28,000 comments so

verification.notes: The official program upload currently has more than 20 million accumulated views, so the broad total is plausible. The stated comment snapshot was not independently recoverable, and a low comment-to-view ratio alone does not establish fabrication; YouTube says engagement metrics can lag, freeze, and be adjusted during validation.

records.text: Turning Point USA's alternative halftime campaign failed to draw viewers away from the NFL.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This means that the, I would say, unnecessary Super Bowl political lines that were drawn ... by Turning Point USA was not successful in terms of drawing people away from the NFL's viewership. Now, in case you missed it, when Bad Bunny was announced,

verification.notes: Nielsen's finalized measurement shows the NFL halftime audience averaged 128.2 million, above the full-game average of 125.6 million, while AP observed roughly 5 million concurrent viewers on TPUSA's YouTube stream. These figures support that the NFL retained an overwhelmingly larger audience, but public aggregate counts cannot prove that no viewers were drawn away or establish the counterfactual audience without the alternative.

records.text: The All-American Halftime Show was filmed weeks in advance in Fayetteville, Georgia, with only 180 audience members who were moved around for camera tricks to make the room look full.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: The person said, first and foremost, this was filmed, which we have already told you, and they've said two weeks ago or weeks leading up to it in Fayetteville, Georgia. There were actually only 180 people in the audience and they used camera tricks to make it look like it was really filled. They were just moved around the room to make it look more full

verification.notes: Transcript context attributes production details to anonymous participant messages. Independent reporting confirms the show was prerecorded at a studio outside Atlanta and performed before approximately 200 people, close to the claimed 180. Searches did not independently confirm Fayetteville, the exact count, filming weeks, or moving audience members for camera tricks.

records.text: Performers at the All-American Halftime Show did three to five takes per song, except Gabby Barrett, who completed hers in two.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: They were just moved around the room to make it look more full and they had to do about three to five takes each on every song, except for Gabby (Gabby Barrett). They said she got it done in two.

verification.notes: Transcript context attributes the take counts to anonymous private participant messages. Live searches confirmed the show was prerecorded and found Kid Rock discussing a production flub, but no call sheet, raw footage, performer account, or reliable report established three-to-five takes per song or exactly two for Gabby Barrett.

records.text: Participants did not know they were signing up for a split halftime show until they arrived, many liked Bad Bunny, and they had expected a bigger artist who could rival the Super Bowl halftime performance.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: They had no idea what they were signing up for. The majority of the people didn't even agree once they got. They got there and were told with doing a split halftime show, a lot of them actually liked Bad Bunny as a bad buddy. ... they also thought that it was going to be a bigger artist because they were told that they were going to contend with the halftime show and they didn't think that they were going to do that

verification.notes: Transcript context attributes participants' expectations and preferences to anonymous messages. Searches found public reports about the announced alternative show and its performers but no authenticated participant interviews or production records proving they learned the format only on arrival, liked Bad Bunny, or expected a larger artist.

records.text: Erika Kirk was not present during either of the All-American Halftime Show's two filming days, which participants found strange.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: it was over two days of filming monday and a tuesday and they were kind of shocked that Erika (Erika Kirk) was not present at all for that filming they did not meet her they felt like it was very weird

verification.notes: Transcript context relies on anonymous participant messages. Current sources show Erika Kirk did not appear on stage and promoted the show beforehand, but absence from the broadcast does not prove she was absent from both filming days. No production attendance record or attributable participant account was found.

records.text: All-American Halftime Show participants worked 12-hour days for a $250 stipend, and the production ran out of food on the first day.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: They told me they were very tired because these were 12-hour days. They were compensated $250 stipend for that. They ran out of food. On the first day

verification.notes: Transcript context relies on anonymous participant messages. Live searches found no public contract, casting notice, pay record, production schedule, catering record, or attributable participant testimony confirming 12-hour days, a 50 stipend, or food running out.

records.text: Halftime-show participants sometimes waited for hours without communication, performers were late, they waited longest for Kid Rock, and Gabby Barrett was early.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #3 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: There was a holding room in between the takes and they felt that there was no communication of why they were waiting for hours sometimes there were technical problems they also had the performers themselves were late and they were not told why they were kind of in this holding space and except for Gabby Barrett they said that she was early and she only needed to do her song twice so she was the strong exception they waited the longest for Kid Rock

verification.notes: Transcript context relies on anonymous participant messages about holding-room delays and performer punctuality. Searches found no production log, call sheet, raw schedule, or attributable participant or performer account that could verify hours-long waits, who was late, or the relative timing of Kid Rock and Gabby Barrett.

records.text: A source told us President Trump would watch the All-American Halftime Show and that it would get more views than Bad Bunny's halftime show.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #6 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: the person who was producing this, some guy named Matt (halftime-show producer; surname unverified) was trying to get them hyped by saying there's a little birdie that told us that Trump (Donald J. Trump) is going to be watching our halftime show. ... he also said to them that this is going to get more views than the Bad Bunny halftime show

verification.notes: Transcript context relays a producer's prediction that Trump would watch and the show would beat Bad Bunny. Current results directly contradict the prediction: Trump publicly reviewed Bad Bunny's official show, and Nielsen measured 128.2 million viewers for it versus roughly 5 million concurrent YouTube viewers for TPUSA's show.

Live searches found no hotel invoices, rooming list, participant agreement, NDA, or attributable production source confirming covered rooms, random roommate assignment, the Kid Rock instruction, or the NDA's one-hour expiration.
